summary: Each new term is the sum of products of every pair of distinct digits of the current term. We keep going until the term is a single digit, adding every term (including N) to a total (T2 — digit manipulation, with `itertools.combinations`).

blocks.title: Import the pair generator
blocks.text: `combinations(items, 2)` gives every pair exactly once, in order — no double loop and no pair counted twice.

blocks.title: Read N
blocks.text: One whole number. Python ints have no size limit, so big N is fine.

blocks.title: Compute the next term
blocks.text: `set(str(x))` keeps each digit once (the problem says distinct digits, so 55 has no pairs → 0). `sorted` just gives a fixed order. The digits are characters, so each one goes through `int()` before multiplying.

blocks.title: Start the total with N itself
blocks.text: N is the first term of the sequence, so it is counted before any step. Forgetting it is the most common wrong answer here.

blocks.title: Repeat until a single digit
blocks.text: `while cur >= 10` means "while it still has 2 or more digits". Each new term is added to the total, including the final single digit.

complexity: Very fast: after one step the value is at most 870, so only a handful of steps run.
pitfalls: Using all digits instead of distinct digits.
